lines.trans: When you cannot solve a problem, you only have one way out.

words.gloss: there is (у меня есть = I have)

lines.trans: To forget it forever and
try to live on.
Defendant Denis Andreyevich Krylov, you are accused of infidelity.
But it is not my fault!
Right now it is going to get even better.
Arousal denied.
My stomach cramped up.
I need the toilet, it is a total nightmare in there.
Could you not hold it for at least an hour?
At least five minutes.
When our housemates are not home, we will be running all night.

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'andreyevich' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Степан Андреевич заболел, к нам нельзя.
examples.trans: Stepan Andreyevich got sick, so he can't come home.
Stepan Andreyevich?

meanings.en: to run (in various directions or habitually)
meanings.note: вокруг меня бегала = she was running after me

examples.trans: She was running after me.
The children are running around in the yard.

examples.text: Это она со мной познакомилась! Вокруг меня бегала.
examples.trans: She was the one who came up to me! She was running after me.

meanings.note: with a past-tense verb: я бы подумал = I would think
wishes: купили бы = we could have bought

examples.trans: I would think about it.
I'd buy a house.

examples.text: Я бы на твоём месте подумал.
examples.trans: If I were you, I'd think about it.

meanings.note: the present tense is normally left out: я мэр = I am the mayor
Present есть; у меня есть = I have. Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to be; there is'.
future: буду / будешь ... + infinitive

examples.trans: I have a toy car.
Childhood was hard.
You will be asking for forgiveness.

meanings.note: + prepositional (where). Core Russian prep meaning 'in, into' in everyday speech.
+ accusative (where to). Core Russian prep meaning 'in, into' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: How is it in Hungary?
I grew up in a communal flat.
Hello! How was it in Hungary?

meanings.note: The neuter form 'всё' used alone. Core Russian det meaning 'all, whole; everyone, everything' in everyday speech.
Neuter всё. Core Russian det meaning 'all, whole; everyone, everything' in everyday speech.
Plural все. Core Russian det meaning 'all, whole; everyone, everything' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: Everything's fine.
As you all know...
Share with everyone.

meanings.note: Common feminine noun meaning 'hanger / total nightmare' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: На кухне отеля всегда есть вешалка.
examples.trans: In the hotel kitchen there is always hanger.
The chef immediately noticed where the hanger was.

meanings.note: usually short form: я виноват / я виновата

examples.trans: I know it's my fault.

examples.text: Она ни в чём не виновата.
examples.trans: She is not to blame for anything.

examples.text: Пожалуйста, не гони меня. Я знаю, что я виноват.
examples.trans: Please, don't chase me away. I know it's my fault.

meanings.note: Verbal action/result neuter noun formed with '-ение'/'-ание'. Common neuter noun meaning 'initiation / arousal' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: На кухне отеля всегда есть возбуждение.
examples.trans: In the hotel kitchen there is always initiation.
The chef immediately noticed where the initiation was.

meanings.note: In 'до встречи' = until we meet. Common feminine noun meaning 'meeting' in everyday Russian.
In 'до встречи' = until we meet. Common feminine noun meaning 'meeting' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: See you!
I have a meeting.

examples.text: Решается ваш вопрос, Клавдия Викторовна! Вы не видите, у меня встреча?
examples.trans: Your question is being sorted out, Klavdia Viktorovna! Can't you see I have a meeting?

meanings.note: polite to one person, or to several people

meanings.en: other forms: вас (gen/acc), вам (dat), вами (instr), вас (prep)
meanings.note: Case forms. Core Russian pron meaning 'you (polite or plural)' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: As you all know...
Does the governor support you?

examples.text: Спасибо, спасибо! Как вы все знаете, я родился и вырос в Синеозерске.
examples.trans: Thank you, thank you! As you all know, I was born and grew up in Sineozersk.

meanings.note: выход всегда есть = there's always a way out
выход всегда есть = there's always a way out

examples.trans: There's always a way out.
Where is the exit?

examples.text: Как говорит наш губернатор, выход всегда есть.
examples.trans: As our governor says, there's always a way out.

meanings.note: In a list or a story. Core Russian adv meaning 'next; further' in everyday speech.
In a list or a story. Core Russian adv meaning 'next; further' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: All right. Next.
What's next?

examples.text: А дальше? Я очень волнуюсь, я к этому не приспособлена.
examples.trans: And then what? I'm very nervous, I'm not cut out for this.

meanings.note: + genitive. Core Russian prep meaning 'until, before; up to' in everyday speech.
Core Russian prep meaning 'until, before; up to' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: Goodbye!
See you tomorrow!
See you tonight!

related.gloss: to reach, walk as far as

meanings.note: Location; compare домой = homeward. Core Russian adv meaning 'at home' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: The main thing is, you keep him at home.
Today I'm staying at home.

examples.text: А Осипенко сейчас дома лежит. У него больное сердце.
examples.trans: And Osipenko is lying at home right now. He has a sick heart.

meanings.note: in threats: ты ещё увидишь = you'll see
Core Russian adv meaning 'more; still; yet' in everyday speech.
Ещё больше = even more. Core Russian adv meaning 'more; still; yet' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: You've still got some.
You'll be sorry!

examples.text: У тебя же есть ещё. Дай хоть одну.
examples.trans: But you've still got some. Give me just one.

meanings.note: у меня болит живот = I have a stomach ache
у меня болит живот = I have a stomach ache

examples.trans: He has a big belly.
My stomach hurts.

examples.text: Живот у тебя, как у депутата.
examples.trans: You've got a belly like a member of parliament.

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to live'.

examples.trans: I live in a communal flat.
I want to live normally.

examples.text: Я хочу нормально жить! Я хочу биде, понимаешь?
examples.trans: I want to live like a normal person! I want a bidet, do you understand?

meanings.note: Used as a perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to forget', paired with 'забывать'.

examples.trans: Don't forget to wash the toilet.
I forgot the keys.

examples.text: Сейчас будешь чинить трубу. И унитаз не забудь помыть.
examples.trans: Now you're going to fix the pipe. And don't forget to wash the toilet.

meanings.note: emphasis: вот поэтому ты и... = that's exactly why you...

examples.trans: I was born and grew up here.
Dad and Mum.

examples.text: Спасибо, спасибо! Как вы все знаете, я родился и вырос в Синеозерске.
examples.trans: Thank you, thank you! As you all know, I was born and grew up in Sineozersk.

meanings.note: Common feminine noun meaning 'betrayals / infidelities' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Ты знаешь, я ведь сильно изменилась.
examples.trans: You know, I have changed a lot, after all.
You know, I have changed.

examples.text: Начать новую жизнь без тебя и твоих измен!
examples.trans: To start a new life without you and your infidelities!

meanings.note: declines like какой: какая-то, какое-то, какие-то

examples.text: Бред какой-то. Но, с другой стороны, чем я рискую?
examples.trans: What nonsense. But on the other hand, what have I got to lose?

meanings.note: Question word and conjunction. Core Russian adv meaning 'when' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: When?
When I grow up, I'll be the mayor.
Oh yeah? When?

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'Krylov' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: На кухне отеля всегда есть крылов.
examples.trans: In the hotel kitchen there is always Krylov.
The chef immediately noticed where the Krylov was.

meanings.note: Comparative of хорошо. Core Russian adv meaning 'better' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: It's better like this.
I feel better today.
Working. Making people's lives better.

meanings.note: Common feminine noun meaning 'minute' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: I'll be there in ten minutes.
Just a minute!

examples.text: Ладно, будь там. Через десять минут буду.
examples.trans: All right, stay there. I'll be there in ten minutes.

meanings.note: + infinitive. Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'can, to be able', paired with 'смочь'.

examples.trans: I can't today.
That can't be.

examples.text: Этого не может быть. Это наша история.
examples.trans: That can't be. It's our history.
Leave this place forever!
They parted forever.
Say that you are leaving for good.

meanings.note: наш, наша, наше, наши; agrees with the noun

examples.trans: I love our town.
This is our flat.

examples.text: Я очень люблю наш город. Поэтому я иду на второй срок.
examples.trans: I love our town very much. That's why I'm running for a second term.

meanings.note: goes right before the word it negates

examples.trans: I don't know.
There wasn't enough money.
Chef, I didn't take it.

meanings.note: Stronger contrast than 'а'. Core Russian conj meaning 'but' in everyday speech.

examples.text: Мы сделали много, но надо ещё.
examples.trans: We've done a lot, but we need more.
I want to, but I can't.

examples.text: Мы сделали много, но надо сделать ещё больше.
examples.trans: We've done a lot, but we need to do even more.

meanings.note: ночью = at night; спокойной ночи = good night

examples.trans: Good night!
At night I sleep.

examples.text: Ну что, Аркаша? Наступила ночь, просыпается мафия.
examples.trans: So, Arkasha? Night has fallen, the mafia wakes up.

meanings.note: Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'is accused'.

examples.text: Надо всё сделать и обвиняться вовремя.
examples.trans: We need to do everything and is accused on time.

examples.text: На нашей кухне все умеют обвиняться.
examples.trans: In our kitchen everyone knows how to is accused.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian pronominal determiner meaning 'one', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Нам очень дорого обходится авторская кухня.
examples.trans: Auteur cuisine costs us very dearly.

examples.text: Это все, кто выходил из отеля.
examples.trans: That is everyone who left the hotel.
What is going on here right now?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'to her', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Она нашла нас на новом месте.
examples.trans: She found us at the new place.
That is it, she got really offended.
She is not answering her phone.

meanings.note: + dative (кому). Prefix 'от-' ('away from, off') marks separation, completion, or response (stem 'казать'). Used as a perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to refuse, to turn down', paired with 'отказывать'.

examples.text: Марина, послушайте, это я вам отказал!
examples.trans: Marina, listen, I was the one who turned you down!
They turned him down in court.

examples.text: Я мерзкий? Марина, послушайте, это я вам отказал!
examples.trans: I'm disgusting? Marina, listen, I was the one who turned you down!

meanings.note: declined like a masculine adjective

examples.trans: The defendant stood up.
The defendant's health.

examples.text: Конфликты с соседями угрожают здоровью подсудимого.
examples.trans: Conflicts with the neighbours threaten the defendant's health.

meanings.note: Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'пытаться'). Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as a perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to try, attempt'.

examples.trans: To try to convince you.

examples.text: Надо всё сделать и попытаться вовремя.
examples.trans: We need to do everything and to try on time.

потерпеть.gloss: to be patient for a while, to endure

meanings.en: to be patient for a little while, to hold on
meanings.note: Often imperative: потерпи!. Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'терпеть'). Used as a perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to be patient for a while, to endure', paired with 'терпеть'.

examples.text: Нам нужно чуть-чуть потерпеть и немножко поработать.
examples.trans: We need to be patient a little and work a bit.
Hang on for five more minutes.

examples.text: Послушай меня, Ваня. Нам нужно чуть-чуть потерпеть и немножко поработать.
examples.trans: Listen to me, Vanya. We need to be patient a little and work a bit.

meanings.note: Prefix 'при-' indicates approaching, attachment, or slight degree of action (stem 'хватить'). Used as a perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'brought along'.

examples.text: Я тут пару друзей с собой прихватил.
examples.trans: I brought a couple of friends along with me here.

examples.text: Надо всё сделать и прихватить вовремя.
examples.trans: We need to do everything and brought along on time.

meanings.note: 'будут проблемы' = there'll be trouble

examples.trans: That's not a problem.
I have a problem.
I know the problems of ordinary people.

meanings.note: + genitive plural: пять рублей. Core Russian num meaning 'five' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: Five thousand roubles.
I'm five years old.

examples.text: Мы же только начинаем. Через месяц будет пять тысяч.
examples.trans: But we're only just starting. In a month there'll be five thousand.

meanings.note: + infinitive: решил стать = decided to become
Решить задачу. Used as a perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to decide; to solve', paired with 'решать'.

examples.trans: The court has decided.
I've decided.

examples.text: Суд решил: домашний арест по месту прописки.
examples.trans: The court has decided: house arrest at his registered address.

meanings.note: 'сейчас буду' = I'll be right there

examples.trans: I'm in the office now.
I'll be right there.

examples.text: Конечно, помогу. Кто у вас сейчас начальник?
examples.trans: Of course I'll help. Who's your boss now?

meanings.note: Agent/instrument noun formed with the productive Slavic suffix '-тель' ('-er'). Common masculine noun meaning 'of roommates / partners' in everyday Russian.

meanings.note: At the start of a question. Core Russian part meaning 'so, then; like that' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: Everything's fine there.
Who's there?
Hello! How was it in Hungary?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'that', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Our restaurant is located right here.

examples.text: Мы теперь работаем в этом отеле.
examples.trans: We now work in this hotel.
How does a hotel restaurant differ?

meanings.note: softens a request: только не сердись = just don't be angry

examples.trans: I was only looking.
Just one.
I was only looking!

meanings.note: The room or the bowl. Common masculine noun meaning 'toilet' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: Where's the toilet?
The toilet is in the corridor.
Do you remember the toilet in the communal flat?

meanings.note: One person, informal. Core Russian pron meaning 'you (informal)' in everyday speech.

meanings.en: other forms: тебя (gen/acc), тебе (dat), тобой (instr), тебе (prep)
meanings.note: Case forms. Core Russian pron meaning 'you (informal)' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: Hi! Look what I've got.

хотя.gloss: even if, at least (with бы); although

meanings.note: нужно хотя бы поговорить = we need at least to talk
Core Russian part meaning 'even if, at least (with бы); although' in everyday speech.

examples.text: Нужно хотя бы поговорить с ними.
examples.trans: We need at least to talk with them.
Have at least some tea.

examples.text: Вы плохо поступили, но хотя бы совесть есть.
examples.trans: You acted badly, but at least you have a conscience.

meanings.note: Formed with a diminutive/expressive Slavic suffix adding warmth or small scale. Common masculine noun meaning 'an hour or so' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: На кухне отеля всегда есть часик.
